first_failures.result: The original workflow encryption field was rejected. The final native CLI preview resolves exact recipient/subkey/profile and destination without contact, then ordinary reviewed execution sends ciphertext independently decrypted and verified by GnuPG.

Ordinary delivery-work had no configured retained-byte quota and refused ciphertext acceptance. Both CLI constructors now receive the quota. The exact original intent accepts a durable artifact while its stopped receiver retains retry; the final stock-client journey also completes an ordinary CLI encrypted worker.

fixture_observation.finding: The initial unit fixture asserted expiry without assigning a lifetime. It now explicitly enrolls a one-day key and checks refusal after that actual limit. No production condition, assertion or budget was relaxed.

mechanisms: Explicit encrypt-purpose public registration pins primary and actual selected encryption-subkey fingerprints, profiles, definition hash and effective expiry. Existing verification-only encodings/hashes remain unchanged; no secret key, key fetch or UID-based trust enters execution.

The normal typed SFTP workflow definition and approval bind recipient/profile, destination connection and filename. Run creation freezes the exact accepted source revision. Preview exposes the recipient/subkey without generating bytes or contacting a peer.

Two independent PostgreSQL encryption slots precede transfer admission; they are released before acquiring a transfer slot. Generation is bounded by a 60-second context inside the unchanged 90-second worker deadline, eight-attempt budget, 30-second lease and five-second renewal.

One ciphertext is durably sealed then accepted with its exact event/projection under the live worker fence before opening the receiver. Source, storage UUID, actor authority, current key and approved workflow are rechecked. Source reads are at most 32 KiB; v2 AEAD chunks are 32 KiB.

Generated-byte reservation uses the same global custody advisory lock as ordinary acceptance. Strict ciphertext size/capacity checks retain sealed orphans against quota. Process death releases the reservation; this local serialized profile does not qualify production fairness.
An accepted ciphertext is immutable and reused after restart and a new worker fence. Actual retained bytes are verified before sending; missing/corrupt ciphertext never falls back to plaintext.

Real worker kill after filesystem sync/before SQL acceptance leaves one visible sealed orphan and no accepted artifact. After the unchanged lease expires, another owner accepts a new artifact; orphan bytes never publish.

Remote success with failed local receipt retains publishing/ambiguity and the exact original ciphertext. Same-dispatch replay cannot retransmit uncertain publication; read-only SFTP observation resolves the recorded ciphertext postcondition.

Recipient revocation stops queued/active work and whole-run execution; observed status retains encryption_recipient_unavailable. Explicit recipient rotation requires a new reviewed definition/approval and does not rebind existing jobs.

Run status shows safe ciphertext/provenance metadata. Actor predicates and forced RLS hide other jobs; raw artifact IDs are not downloadable file IDs. Reconciliation recognizes verified/corrupt/missing ciphertext without mutation.

Fresh session keys use protected owned 32-byte buffers with explicit clearing and documented library/runtime limits. Packet cryptography stays in the maintained library. No compression, filename/time hint, hidden recipient, signing key, model or subprocess is used in application encryption.

migration_notes.existing_grants: All preserved. New development administrators still get nineteen explicit grants; recipient execution uses existing workflow/read/deliver authority and key administration requires admin/pgp_manage/root.
migration_notes.sql_guards: Exact event/source/storage/recipient/owner/fence binding, immutable actor-owned artifacts, tenant-aware FKs and deferred approved-workflow encryption/publication/receipt proof.

govulncheck.conclusion: The native source scan retains GO-2026-5932 as a module-only advisory for unimported golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages. No affected package is imported and no reachable symbol is reported. Maintained ProtonMail/go-crypto is a separate module. No zero-advisory or all-platform release claim.

limits: Signed CSV intake followed by explicitly approved recipient encryption and SFTP delivery. Decryption/private signing inside freightctl, malware scanning and complete business acknowledgment remain required.
Independent GnuPG 2.4.9 Linux aarch64 fixture is capped at 128 MiB/one CPU with network disabled; this is not native Linux application qualification.

V4 Ed25519 signature verification; encryption uses Curve25519 and RSA3072 subkeys with AES256 SEIPDv1/MDC GnuPG peers. SEIPDv2/AES256-OCB and v6 have library/unit coverage only; independent peer qualification remains required.

Explicit fingerprint enrollment, frozen source/recipient/destination and durable ciphertext reuse. KMS/HSM, private signing/decryption, delegated review, broader peers/algorithms, remaining encryption/decryption crash boundaries and full journeys remain open.
Historical integrity-only revisions retain their original scope; no retroactive cryptographic verdict is claimed.
Assisted same-host loopback exercise, not production performance, HA, independent adoption or enterprise/release qualification.

Only explicit public recipient-encrypted outbound SFTP is implemented here. Decryption/private signing in freightctl, scanning/ICAP/DLP, general transforms, delegated lifecycle, UI and complete business acknowledgment remain mandatory.

SEIPDv1/MDC uses the older SHA1-based integrity construction with AES256, as explicitly approved. SEIPDv2/AES256-OCB and v6 have library/unit coverage only; independent peer qualification and broader algorithm profiles remain open. No implicit downgrade or FIPS/HSM/KMS claim.

The current single-root generation reservation serializes with ordinary acceptance. Fair quotas, production resource/throughput, large-file, endurance, distributed storage, backup/restore and remaining cancellation/crash boundaries are not qualified.

A revoked workflow/connection/recipient can block read-only recovery until a future governed decision. Already received bytes cannot be recalled. Historical integrity-only and unencrypted revisions retain their explicit scope; no retrospective encryption verdict.
All 83 baseline rows and 12 complete journeys remain open. AI profiles, held-out datasets/evaluations and real inference qualification remain open under X05. No model was started or loaded.
